summary: Defines a way for SIP presence subscribers to receive only the parts of a presence document that changed, instead of the full document each time. By default, any small change causes the whole presence document to be delivered again. This extension reduces that traffic, which helps on slow or constrained networks.

plainLanguage.summary: When a watcher subscribes to someone's presence, the server sends the whole document every time anything in it changes. That is wasteful on a slow link, where the one element that changed may be smaller than the document around it. This document lets the server send only the part that changed.

questions: sip presence event package changes only
how to reduce sip presence notification size
how does sip presence notify work
subtitle: A SIP extension that lets presence servers send only what changed instead of the whole presence document every time.

tldr.problem: When any part of a person's presence document changes, even one element, the presence server delivers a new document with the full set of elements, which wastes bandwidth on slow, high-latency links.
tldr.mechanism: A watcher adds application/pidf-diff+xml to the Accept header of its SUBSCRIBE request. The presence agent then sends a full document first, followed by numbered NOTIFY requests that carry only the added, removed and replaced parts.
tldr.outcome: Less presence data crosses the network, and the watcher keeps a local copy that it updates as the diffs arrive. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 8996.

facts.label: Version step
facts.value: incremented by one per partial notification

today: RFC 5263 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2008. It has not been obsoleted, but it was updated by RFC 8996.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The presence event package for SIP allows users, called watchers, to subscribe to other users' presence information, that is, to the presence of a presentity. The presence information is composed of multiple pieces of data delivered to the watcher, and the size of the presence information document can be large, because the document can contain an arbitrary number of elements called presence tuples that convey data.

As specified in RFC 2778 and in the presence event package for SIP, a Presence Agent always delivers in presence notifications all the presence data that has been authorized for a certain watcher. This is done regardless of what presence data has changed compared to the last notification. It may not be reasonable to send the complete presence information over low bandwidth and high latency links when only part of the presence information has actually changed. This may end up degrading the presence service and causing bad perception at the watcher side.

This document defines a partial notification approach where the presence server delivers to the watchers only those parts of the presence information that have changed compared to the presence information sent in the previous notifications. This reduces the amount of data that is transported over the network. The mechanism utilizes the presence event package for SIP and a new MIME type for carrying partial Presence Information Data Format documents.
sections.plainLanguage: When a watcher subscribes to someone's presence, the server sends the whole document every time anything in it changes. That is wasteful on a slow link, where the one element that changed may be smaller than the document around it. This document lets the server send only the part that changed.

sections.title: Basic Presence Agent Operation
sections.content:
The presence service normally operates so that a watcher sends a SIP SUBSCRIBE request targeted to the presentity. The request is routed to the presence agent, where the presentity's presence information is stored. The SUBSCRIBE request can include an Accept header field that indicates the supported content types.

The presence agent receives the SUBSCRIBE request, and if there is no Accept header indicating the supported content types, or the Accept header contains the default PIDF content type, the presence agent will generate presence notifications using the default PIDF format. The PIDF document can contain one or multiple XML elements, and includes a set of elements defined in RFC 2778 together with its extensions for representing the presence information. This PIDF document is carried in the body of a NOTIFY request. During basic operation, the presence document always contains the full state corresponding to the presence status of the presentity, as determined by the presence agent's local policy and authorization rules.
sections.plainLanguage: In the ordinary case, a watcher subscribes to a person and the server keeps that person's presence information. Every notification carries the whole document, chosen according to the server's policy and the rules about what the watcher is allowed to see.

sections.title: Operation with Partial Notification
sections.content:
The partial notification mechanism allows a watcher to request that, whenever possible, notifications contain only presence information that has actually changed. A watcher that wants to receive partial notifications according to this document creates a SIP SUBSCRIBE request similar to that of a regular presence subscription, but the Accept header field contains the application/pidf-diff+xml tag as well as the application/pidf+xml tag.

When the presence agent receives the subscription, it examines the Accept header field value, and if the application/pidf-diff+xml value is present, it can decide to use the partial notifications mechanism. The presence agent then builds NOTIFY requests with the Content-Type header field set to application/pidf-diff+xml. The first NOTIFY request that contains presence information carries a full presence document, and subsequent NOTIFY requests can carry partial presence documents.
sections.plainLanguage: The watcher asks for the diff format in the Accept header of its subscription. If the server agrees, it sends one complete document first, so the watcher starts from a known state, and after that only the changes.

sections.title: Negotiating the Content Type
sections.content:
Entities supporting the partial notification extension described in this document MUST support the application/pidf-diff+xml content type specified in the PIDF extension for partial presence.

A SUBSCRIBE request can be used to negotiate the preferred content type to be used in the notifications, and the Accept header field is used for this purpose. When a watcher wants to allow the presence agent to send partial notifications, the watcher MUST include an Accept header field in its SUBSCRIBE request, and its value MUST contain application/pidf-diff+xml, in addition to the application/pidf+xml required by the SIP presence event package. The watcher MAY include a q parameter with each Accept value to indicate the relative preference of that value.

The presence agent compares the values included in the Accept header field with the supported ones, and decides which one to use. If the watcher has indicated preferred accept values by means of q parameters, the presence agent SHOULD base the decision on those preferences, unless otherwise indicated by the presence agent's local policy.
sections.plainLanguage: The two formats are negotiated in the Accept header, the same way a browser and a server agree on a file format. The watcher can also say which it prefers, using the q value. The server follows the watcher's preference unless its own policy says otherwise.

sections.title: Presence Agent Generation of Partial Notifications
sections.content:
Once a subscription is accepted and installed, the presence agent MUST deliver the full state of the presence information in the first partial notification that contains a presence document having a pidf-full root element. If the presence agent decides to send notifications that include a presence document according to this specification, it MUST build the presence document according to the PIDF extension for Partial Presence and MUST set the Content-Type header field to the value application/pidf-diff+xml.

The presence agent MUST include a version attribute, and for the first partial notification within a given subscription the version MUST be initialized to the value one. This version counter is scoped to the subscription and is incremented by one within each partial notification. The version value is only reset when the given subscription is terminated, and is not reset when the subscription is refreshed.

The presence agent SHOULD include only the presence information that has changed compared to the previous notifications, and it is up to the presence agent's local policy to determine what is considered a change to the previous state. The document is constructed so that all the information that has been added is listed inside add elements, all information that has been removed is listed inside remove elements, and all information that has been changed is listed under replace elements. The version number MUST be incremented by one compared to the earlier successfully sent presence document to the watcher associated with the subscription.

The presence agent MUST NOT send a new NOTIFY request that contains a partial notification for the same Request-URI until it has received a final response from the watcher for the previous one, or the previous NOTIFY request has timed out. When the presence agent receives a SUBSCRIBE request, whether a refresh or a termination, within the associated subscription, it SHOULD send a NOTIFY request containing the full presence document. If the presence agent has used a content type other than application/pidf-diff+xml within the existing subscription, and changes to delivering partial notifications, it MUST deliver the full state of the presence information as the first partial notification.
sections.plainLanguage: Each partial notification carries a version number that goes up by one, so the watcher can tell whether it missed anything. The body lists what was added, what was removed and what was replaced. Only one partial notification is in flight at a time, and the full document comes back whenever the subscription is refreshed.

sections.title: Watcher Processing of NOTIFY Requests
sections.content:
The watcher processes all NOTIFY requests that contain application/pidf+xml content type as specified in the presence event package for SIP.

When the watcher receives the first notification containing an application/pidf-diff+xml body, it MUST initialize an internal version counter, related to this subscription, to the value of the version included in the presence document, and MUST store the received full presence document as its local copy. For a subsequent document the watcher MUST compare the received version attribute with the local version counter. If the watcher receives a presence document with a version equal to or lower than the locally stored version number, it is considered a presence agent failure, and the watcher SHOULD discard the document without further processing.

Otherwise the watcher MUST modify its locally stored information. If the root element is pidf-full, the watcher replaces its local copy with the document received and sets the internal version to the value of the version attribute. If the root element is pidf-diff and the received version number is incremented by one compared with the local version counter, the watcher MUST apply the changes to its local copy as specified in the PIDF extension for Partial Presence, and MUST increment its local version counter by one. If the root element is pidf-diff and the received version is higher by more than one compared with the locally stored value, the watcher assumes that one or more NOTIFYs were lost, and SHOULD either refresh the subscription in order to receive a full presence document, or terminate the subscription.

If the watcher encounters a processing error while processing the received document, it SHOULD renew the subscription, and MAY fall back to normal presence operations by not inserting application/pidf-diff+xml in a new SUBSCRIBE request. If the presence agent changes the content type used in notifications within the existing subscription, the watcher MUST discard all the previously received presence information, except the local version counter, and process the new content as specified for that content type. The local version counter MUST NOT be discarded, because if the presence agent changes back to application/pidf-diff+xml the version counter will continue to increase from the last value.
sections.plainLanguage: The watcher keeps its own copy of the presence information and its own version number. Each new document is checked against that number: a version that goes up by one is applied to the local copy, a version that goes backwards is thrown away as a server error, and a jump of more than one means a notification was lost, so the watcher asks for a fresh full document or gives up on the subscription.

sections.title: Examples
sections.content: The example message flow shows a watcher that declares support for the default presence format, application/pidf+xml, and for the partial notification format, application/pidf-diff+xml, in the Accept header field value. The watcher uses the q parameter to set the preference for receiving partial notifications. The presence agent accepts the subscription and, based on the q parameter value, selects to send partial notifications in NOTIFY requests. The first NOTIFY request includes the full state of the presence information, and the following notifications only include the difference from the previous NOTIFY requests. Each NOTIFY request is answered by the watcher with a 200 OK.
sections.plainLanguage: The worked example shows one subscription, one full document and one partial document. The watcher marks the diff format as its first preference, and the server follows that.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of the presence event package for SIP apply to this document as well. Issues described in that package, including confidentiality, message integrity and authenticity, outbound authentication, replay prevention, denial-of-service attacks against third parties and denial-of-service attacks against servers, all apply here without any change. It is RECOMMENDED that TLS be used between elements to provide hop-by-hop confidentiality protection, and S/MIME MAY be used for integrity and authenticity of SUBSCRIBE and NOTIFY requests.

The RFC also notes that a third party can inject a NOTIFY request with partial state that will cause the watcher to think it has missed a partial notification and to request a new full presence document. This is no worse than what happens without the extension, because a party that could perform such an action could also send a NOTIFY with a Subscription-State of terminated and achieve the same effect without knowing about the extension. Partial Notification does not make the situation any worse, and the protection mechanisms from the existing system apply to preventing this attack against the partial notification mechanism.
sections.plainLanguage: The security rules of the presence event package apply unchanged. One new point is that someone who can inject a fake notification could make the watcher ask for a full document again, but that party could already end the subscription, so the extension does not make things worse.
